mechanism_narrative: The sharp rebound in WORKPLACES and TRANSIT after mid-September signals a broader return to in-person commuting and downtown trips, which should lift retail visits within four weeks as weekday circulation expands.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise relative to the prior four-week mean even when WORKPLACES and TRANSIT both improve for at least two consecutive weeks.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL stays elevated while TRANSIT remains depressed, households substitute local errands and neighborhood spending for longer discretionary trips, keeping retail-and-recreation mobility lower over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT stays below -25 and RESIDENTIAL stays above +5 week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises over the next 14 days despite TRANSIT remaining below -25 and RESIDENTIAL remaining above +5.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week recovery in GROCERY_PHARM above its recent depressed level indicates loosening demand-side restrictions or reduced risk aversion, which then spills over into broader retail outings within one week.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM rises by at least 4 points week-on-week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not improve in the following week after a weekly increase of at least 4 points in GROCERY_PHARM.

mechanism_narrative: Persistently positive PARKS mobility in warm-weather weeks marks favorable outdoor conditions and social activity, which should slightly pull up discretionary retail visits over a four-week window.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC remains below its prior four-week average even while PARKS stays positive for four straight weeks.

mechanism_narrative: If WORKPLACES drops below its recent trough while TRANSIT does not recover, fewer commuter-linked retail trips occur and RETAIL_REC falls over the following four weeks.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES falls below -45 while TRANSIT stays below -25
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC increases over the next 28 days despite WORKPLACES remaining below -45 and TRANSIT below -25.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained pullback in RESIDENTIAL after several weeks of staying above baseline indicates more time spent outside the home, which should translate into higher retail-and-recreation mobility within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by at least 2 points from its prior week
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days after RESIDENTIAL declines by at least 2 points week-on-week.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated recovery in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES after a soft patch signals easier commuting conditions and fewer access frictions, which should lift discretionary retail mobility over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises above -28 and WORKPLACES rises above -40
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC stays flat or declines over 28 days after both TRANSIT exceeds -28 and WORKPLACES exceeds -40.

mechanism_narrative: In late-summer/early-autumn conditions, rising PARKS mobility and stable-to-improving GROCERY_PHARM reflect active local routines that spill into shopping and leisure visits, raising RETAIL_REC over a one-week horizon.
candidate_trigger: PARKS rises above 8 while GROCERY_PHARM rises above -20
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not increase in the next week when PARKS is above 8 and GROCERY_PHARM is above -20.
